Find ${lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x)^{3}(f(x)-4{x}^{2})^{5}$ for the function $f(x)$ plotted above.
question.worked_solution:
From the graph, we get that ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=3.$ 

From the product rule, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x)^{3}(f(x)-4{x}^{2})^{5}={lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x)^{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,1}(f(x)-4{x}^{2})^{5}.
$$

We calculate the limits of each factor, separately.

Applying the power rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x)^{3} & ={({lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x))}^{3} \\  & =(3-1)^{3} \\  & ={2}^{3} \\  & =8,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,1}(f(x)-4{x}^{2})^{4} & ={({lim}_{x\to \,1}(f(x)-4{x}^{2}))}^{5} \\  & =(3-4(1)^{2})^{5} \\  & =(-1)^{5} \\  & =-1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x)^{3}(f(x)-4{x}^{2})^{5} & ={lim}_{x\to \,1}(3-x)^{3}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,1}(f(x)-4{x}^{2})^{5} \\  & =8\cdot (-1) \\  & =-8\,.\end{aligned}
$$
